subtopics.title: Newton's First Law and the Meaning of Inertia

questions.question: Newton's first law states that an object continues in a state of rest or uniform velocity unless:
options: Any force at all acts on it
It is acted upon by a net or unbalanced force
Friction is removed from the surface
Its mass changes

questions.question: Inertia is best described as:
options: The tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of rest or uniform motion
The force that keeps an object moving
The product of mass and velocity
The friction between an object and a surface

questions.question: When a taxi brakes hard, an unbelted passenger is thrown forward because:
options: A forward force acts on the passenger during braking
The passenger's weight increases as the taxi slows
The seat pushes the passenger forward
No backward force acts on the passenger, so the passenger continues at the original velocity

questions.question: Which statement is FALSE?
options: Mass is the measure of an object's inertia
A loaded bakkie has more inertia than an empty one
A continuous force is needed to keep an object moving at constant velocity
A headrest reduces whiplash by providing the missing force on the head

subtopics.title: Newton's Second Law and the Fnet = ma Method

questions.question: Newton's second law states that the acceleration of an object is:
options: Directly proportional to the mass and inversely proportional to the net force
Directly proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to the mass, in the direction of the net force
Equal to the net force multiplied by the mass
Independent of the direction of the net force

questions.question: A 20 kg crate is pulled horizontally with 100 N while friction on it is 40 N. The acceleration is:
options: 3 m·s⁻² in the direction of the applied force
5 m·s⁻² in the direction of the applied force
2 m·s⁻² opposite to the applied force
60 m·s⁻² in the direction of the applied force

questions.question: To drag that same crate at CONSTANT velocity, the applied force must be:
One newton is defined as:
options: The weight of one kilogram on Earth
The force of gravity on 9,8 kg
One kilogram per metre per second
The net force that gives a mass of 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m·s⁻²

subtopics.title: Vertical Applications — Lifts, Cables and Apparent Weight

questions.question: A 70 kg learner stands on a scale in a lift accelerating upward at 2 m·s⁻². The scale reads:
If the same lift accelerates downward at 2 m·s⁻², the scale reads:
options: 0 N

questions.question: During free fall the scale reads zero. This means:
options: Gravity has switched off
The learner's mass has become zero
The learner's true weight is still 686 N — only the supporting force has vanished
The learner's weight is now 9,8 N

questions.question: A 5 000 kg rocket produces 70 000 N of thrust. Its acceleration at launch is:
options: 14 m·s⁻² upward
9,8 m·s⁻² downward
23,8 m·s⁻² upward
4,2 m·s⁻² upward

subtopics.title: Newton's Third Law and Action-Reaction Pairs

questions.question: Which property is essential to a true action-reaction pair?
options: The two forces act on two different objects
The two forces act on the same object
One force is larger than the other
The forces act one after the other

questions.question: A book rests on a table. The reaction to the book's weight is:
options: The normal force of the table on the book
The book pulling the Earth upward with an equal force
The friction between book and table
The book pushing down on the table

questions.question: Why do action-reaction forces never cancel each other out?
options: Because one is always slightly larger
Because they act at different times
Because they act on different objects and so never appear in the same net-force equation
Because friction absorbs one of them

questions.question: A swimmer moves forward because:
options: The water has less inertia than the swimmer
Her weight pulls her along the surface
Her arms create a vacuum ahead of her
She pushes the water backwards and the water pushes her forwards with an equal force

subtopics.title: Why You Jerk Forward When the Taxi Brakes

questions.question: The seatbelt's real job during a sudden stop is to:
options: Supply the backward force your body would otherwise never receive
Increase your inertia so you slow down naturally
Hold you in place while the taxi is standing still
Reduce your mass during the collision

questions.question: A loaded trolley is harder to start and stop than an empty one because it has:
options: Less friction
More inertia, because it has more mass
A larger weight but the same inertia
More acceleration

questions.question: A soccer ball keeps rolling on smooth ground because:
options: A forward force keeps acting on it
It stores the kick inside itself as a force
Nothing much is stopping it — no force is needed to keep it moving
Its inertia pushes it forward

questions.question: The "leftover push" in the lesson is the everyday name for:
options: The applied force
The weight
The friction
The net force

questions.question: Pull of 100 N, friction of 40 N, mass of 20 kg. The acceleration is found by:
Reading "the object moves at constant velocity" should immediately tell you that:
options: The applied force is the largest force present
The net force is zero and all the forces balance
Friction is zero
The acceleration equals the velocity

questions.question: Which habit is recommended before starting any Newton's second law calculation?
options: Convert every force to kilograms
Add the vertical and horizontal forces together
Choose and state a positive direction, and keep the two directions separate
Assume friction is negligible

subtopics.title: The Lift Floor and the Wall That Pushes Back

questions.question: A bathroom scale in a lift is really measuring:
options: Your mass in kilograms
Your true weight, always
How hard the floor has to push up on your feet
The lift's acceleration in metres per second squared

questions.question: As a lift starts moving upward, the scale reading:
options: Rises, because the floor must push extra to accelerate you upward
Falls, because you are moving away from the Earth
Stays the same, because your weight is unchanged
Drops to zero

questions.question: Walking is possible because:
options: Your weight pushes you forward
You push backwards on the ground and the ground pushes you forwards
Friction pushes you backwards
Your inertia carries you forward

questions.question: The horse-and-cart puzzle is resolved by noticing that:
options: The horse pulls harder than the cart pulls back
Friction on the cart is always zero
The cart's pull on the horse acts later in time
The two forces land on different objects, so they never appear in the same net-force sum
